## Raw data

**Data used:**

TMB and Immunotherapy from cBioPortal for cancer genomics

by (MSK, Nat Genet 2019)

[![](images/clipboard-3840736939.png){fig-align="left"}](https://www.cbioportal.org/datasets)

3 files:

-   Patient data

-   Sample data

-   Mutation data

1661 patients represented in data set

## Data cleaning

::: column
-   Selected variables of interest in all three data sets

-   Renamed columns using "snake_case"

-   Changed variable types to factors (age_group and chromosome)

-   Joined patients and samples table by patient_id
:::

::: column
``` r
# Factors
patients_clean <- patients_clean |> 
              mutate(age_group = factor(age_group,
                                        levels = c("<30",
                                                  "31-50",
                                                  "50-60",
                                                  "61-70",
                                                  ">71")))

mutations_clean <- mutations_clean |> 
                mutate(patient_id = str_sub(Tumor_Sample_Barcode, 
                                            start = 1, 
                                            end = 9)) |> 
                mutate(tumor_barcode = str_sub(Tumor_Sample_Barcode, 
                                                      start = 11),
                       .keep = "unused") |> ...
```
:::

## Data wrangling

**Mutation placement**

2 columns: "end_position" and "start_position" -\> length_mutation

``` r
mutation_augment <- mutations |>
  mutate(length_mutation = end_position - start_position,
         is_top_gene = hugo_symbol %in% top_genes)
```

## Survival rate

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
-   Skin Cancer, Non-Melanoma

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))


clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(cancer_type, sex) |> 
  summarise(number_of_patients = n(),
  average_survival = mean(os_months, na.rm = TRUE),
  alive = sum(status == 'LIVING', na.rm = TRUE),
  survival_percent = alive / number_of_patients * 100,
  .groups = 'drop') |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = cancer_type,
                       y = survival_percent,
                       fill = sex)) + 
  geom_col(position = 'dodge')+
  labs (title = 'Survival percentage for each cancer type',
        x = 'Cancer type',
        y = 'Survival percent (%)')+
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(
    angle = 20,
    hjust = 0.75),
    legend.position = 'bottom')

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   Glioma

-   Melanoma
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
survival_curve_test <- clinical_augment |> 
  group_by(cancer_type,os_months) |> 
  summarise(
    deaths = sum(status == 'DECEASED'),
    living = sum(status == 'LIVING'),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |> 
  
  arrange(cancer_type,os_months) |> 
  
  group_by(cancer_type) |> 
  mutate(
    at_risk = rev(cumsum(rev(deaths + living))),
    survival = cumprod(1 - deaths/at_risk)
  ) |> 
  ungroup()


#survival curve for all the cancer types
g1 <- ggplot(data = survival_curve_test,
             
             mapping = aes(x = os_months,
                           y = survival,
                           color = cancer_type))+
  geom_step()+
  labs(title = 'Overall survival curve, by cancer type',
       x = 'Overall survival (months)',
       y = 'Survival probability',
       color = 'Cancer types')+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = 'bottom')+
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      title.position ='top'))
g1

#survival curve for only 2 cancer types - the lowest and one of the higest survival rate
g1 <- ggplot(data = survival_curve_test |> 
             filter(cancer_type %in% c('Melanoma','Glioma')),
             mapping = aes(x = os_months,
                           y = survival,
                           color = cancer_type))+
  geom_step()+
  labs(title = 'Overall survival curve, by extrimaties',
       x = 'Overall survival (months)',
       y = 'Survival probability',
       color = 'Cancer types')+
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = 'bottom')
g1
```

```{r}
library(here)
library(gt)

readRDS(here("data", "summary_lm.rds")) |>
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-align: right

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))

patient_mutation_summary <- clinical_mutation |> 
                              select(patient_id, length_mutation, status, total_mutations, os_months, cancer_type)|> 
                              filter(status == "DECEASED") |> 
                              group_by(patient_id, os_months, total_mutations, cancer_type) |> 
                              summarize(mean_length_mutation = mean(length_mutation),
                                        max_length_mutation = max(length_mutation))

patient_mutation_summary |> 
    filter(cancer_type == "Renal Cell Carcinoma") |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = mean_length_mutation,
               y = os_months))+
    geom_point(alpha = 0.5)+
    geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
    labs(x = "Average length of mutation",
         y = "Survival (months)",
         title = "Survival as a function of average mutation length in patients with Renal Cell Carcinoma")+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 12))
```

## PCA

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))

mutation_matrix <- clinical_augment |>
  select(starts_with("num_mut_"))

pca_fit <- mutation_matrix |>
  prcomp(center = TRUE,
         scale. = TRUE)

pca_variance <- tibble(pc = seq_along(pca_fit$sdev),
                       variance = pca_fit$sdev^2) |>
  mutate(pct_variance = variance / sum(variance) * 100)

# PCA scores
pca_scores <- clinical_augment |>
  select(patient_id, cancer_type, status, total_mutations) |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(pca_fit$x))

pc1_label <- str_c("PC1 (", round(pca_variance$pct_variance[1], 1), "%)")
pc2_label <- str_c("PC2 (", round(pca_variance$pct_variance[2], 1), "%)")

pca_scores |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1,
             y = PC2,
             color = cancer_type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = pc1_label,
       y = pc2_label,
       color = "Cancer type",
       title = "PCA of mutation counts in the top 20 genes")
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
pca_scores |>
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1,
             y = PC2,
             color = status)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = pc1_label,
       y = pc2_label,
       color = "Survival status",
       title = "PCA of mutation counts in the top 20 genes")
```

```{r}
             y = PC2,
             fill = cancer_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha=0.6) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(x = "Cancer type",
       y = "PC2",
       title = "PC2 in melanoma vs colorectal cancer")
```

## Heatmap

```{r}
# Load the augmented data
load(here("data", "03_cancer_augment.RData"))

# Reshape to long format and calculate mutation percentage per cancer type
heatmap_data <- clinical_augment |>
  # Gather all 20 num_mut_* columns into two columns: 'gene' and 'mut_count'
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("num_mut_"),
    names_to = "gene",
    values_to = "mut_count"
  ) |>
  # Clean up the gene names by removing the "num_mut_" prefix
  mutate(gene = str_remove(gene, "^num_mut_")) |>
  # Group by cancer type and gene
  group_by(cancer_type, gene) |>
  # Calculate the % of samples in that cancer type that have at least 1 mutation
  summarise(
    n_samples = n(),
    n_mutated = sum(mut_count > 0),
    pct_mutated = (n_mutated / n_samples) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

heatmap_data |>
  # Order genes so the most frequently mutated ones appear at the top
  mutate(gene = fct_reorder(gene, pct_mutated, .fun = mean)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = cancer_type, y = gene, fill = pct_mutated)) +
  # Draw the heatmap tiles with thin white borders
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # Add exact percentage numbers inside the tiles
  geom_text(aes(label = round(pct_mutated, 0)), size = 2.8, color = "black") +
  # Use a clean color gradient from light to dark
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#f7fbff",
    high = "#08519c",
    name = "Mutated\nSamples (%)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mutation Frequency of Top 20 Driver Genes Across Cancer Types",
    subtitle = "Values inside tiles indicate percentage (%) of samples with ≥1 mutation",
    x = "Cancer Type",
    y = "Driver Gene"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```
